en.html:
Panic, don't panic. Time had no interest. School opened. Lessons happened. The whole timetable went on behaving as though it were reasonable.

A friend disappears, but history has booked the classroom. Kindly keep your personal catastrophe between the bells.

I was in no condition to listen properly. But disappear from class now, and we would only create more worry. 'I'm going to find Ritsu' was not going to get me permission.

The school, and especially the Kurusunos—I didn't want to trouble them. Uncle and Auntie were looking after an orphan who was only a distant relative. Itna they had done for me. How could I make them worry as well?

...If my own parents had raised me, would I go to them at a time like this? Ask for help, just like that?

Pata nahin. I couldn't even remember their faces. An accident, I had been told. That was how they died.

Toh, the best available course: wait until school finished. Then act.

The lesson... sorry, sir. Suzukawa was probably feeling much as we did and still doing his duty. But today, listening was not something I could promise him. My ears would remain in attendance. Anything beyond that was between him and the ears.

Panic, don't panic. Time had no interest. School opened. Lessons happened. The whole timetable went on behaving as though it were reasonable.

A friend disappears, but history has booked the classroom. Kindly keep your personal catastrophe between the bells.

I was in no condition to listen properly. But disappear from class now, and we would only create more worry. 'I'm going to find Ritsu' was not going to get me permission.

The school, and especially the Kurusunos—I didn't want to trouble them. Uncle and Auntie were looking after an orphan who was only a distant relative. Itna they had done for me. How could I make them worry as well?

...If my own parents had raised me, would I go to them at a time like this? Ask for help, just like that?

Pata nahin. I couldn't even remember their faces. An accident, I had been told. That was how they died.

Toh, the best available course: wait until school finished. Then act.

The lesson... sorry, sir. Suzukawa was probably feeling much as we did and still doing his duty. But today, listening was not something I could promise him. My ears would remain in attendance. Anything beyond that was between him and the ears.

ja.html:
焦ろうがのんびりしていようが時間は普通に流れる
し、学校は普通にあるし、授業は普通に行われる。

　正直、授業なんかまともに聞いていられる気分では
なかったが、この状況でさぼったりすれば騒ぎを助長
してしまう。
　リツを探しに行くと断っても通るわけがない。

　学校と、特にご厄介になっている来栖野家に迷惑を
掛けることは避けたかった。
　遠縁の孤児に過ぎないおれの面倒をみてくれている
おじさんおばさんを心配させるわけにはいかない。

　……実の両親に育てられている身なら、こういう時
はむしろ、頼ろうとするのだろうか？
　などとちらりと考えたが、わからなかった。事故で
死んだ（と聞く）両親のことは顔も覚えていない。

　何にせよおれは最善の手段、放課後を待っての行動
を選ぶしかなかった。
　授業は……同じような心境だろうに責務を果たして
いる鈴川には申し訳ないが、聞き流させてもらう。

en.html:
Suzukawa"...Ancient, medieval, early modern, modern, contemporary. History keeps happening. Dividing it into pieces we can manage is called periodization."
Suzukawa"Until last time, modern history. From today, contemporary. Haan, two different names. Where to separate them—"
Suzukawa"On that, people do not agree. Several views exist. One puts the beginning of the contemporary age at the birth of the new-type tsurugi."
Suzukawa"From antiquity right up to now, the tsurugi has been the strongest weapon. It raises the wearer's physical ability enormously and lets a human being fly freely. Better than this, we have still not produced. Progress is trying. Tsurugi is not cooperating."
Suzukawa"Tanks on land, flying ships in the air—powerful weapons, both attracting attention. Achchha, very powerful. But in raw fighting strength, still far below the tsurugi."
Suzukawa"Work on bringing them down continues. HVAP: high-velocity armor-piercing ammunition. Our wartime railgun project also had its period of great attention. Attention se goli nahin chalti. Being talked about does not make a weapon work. Almost none of these projects have reached practical use."
Suzukawa"No weapon that can defeat a tsurugi. No weapon that cannot be defeated by one. A wearer, if so inclined, can wipe out a hundred fully armed infantry. One against a hundred, and the hundred have the problem."
Suzukawa"...No. Even that is not enough. Some, it seems, can destroy a town alone."
Suzukawa"Legends like that, every country has. We citizens of Yamato have the particular misfortune of not being able to leave them in the storybook. Sach mein, a threat we must take seriously. Very unfortunate people we are."
Yuhi"..."

鈴川「……歴史を古代、中世、近世、近代、現代 のように区分けすることを時代区分という」
鈴川「前回まで学んでいたのが近代。 　今日から現代に入るが……」
鈴川「近代、現代の区分には諸説ある。 　その一つは新型劔冑の誕生をもって現代の 始まりとするものだ」
鈴川「上古の時代から今に至るまで、劔冑ツルギは常に 最強の兵器だった。着用した人間の身体能力 を飛躍的に向上させ、空を自在に駆けさせる ……これに勝る武器は未だない」
鈴川「陸上では戦車、空では飛行艦が有力な兵器 として注目されているが……いずれも単純な 戦闘力ではまだまだ劔冑に及ばないというの が実情だ」
鈴川「高速徹甲弾ＨＶＡＰを始め、劔冑の撃墜を目指した 兵器の研究もされている。我が国でも戦時中、 電磁加速砲レールガン計画などが一時期脚光を浴びたな。 　しかし実用に達した例はほとんどない」
鈴川「劔冑を打倒できる兵器は無く、劔冑に打倒 されない兵器も無し。 　そのつもりになれば、劔冑を使う者は一人 で完全武装の歩兵百人を駆逐する事ができる」
鈴川「……いや。それどころか。 　中には、町・をただ一人で壊滅させてしまう 者さえいるようだ」
鈴川「その種の伝説なら何処の国にもあるが…… 　こんな話を、昔の御伽噺ではなく、現実的 な脅威として受け止めなくてはならない我々 大和国民は……残念ながら、非常に不運だな」
雄飛「……」

...Shukr hai. Nothing seemed to be there.

Nothing silver.

en.html:
Suzukawa"That much power, the tsurugi possesses. Its user is called a musha."
Suzukawa"Before the modern age, these warriors came only from a handful of upper warrior families. Takano. Why only so few?"
Takano"Because tsurugi were precious, sir."
Suzukawa"Haan. Now why precious? One more step, beta."
Takano"One smith could make only one."
Suzukawa"Correct. One forging in a lifetime. To finish the armor, the smith must hammer his own body and soul into it. 'Passing through the shingane'—the heart-steel."
Suzukawa"Only then does it gain that supreme power, and a brain to control the power according to its user's will. Without the heart-steel? Very fine armor. Bas, armor. You may admire the workmanship while remaining firmly on the ground."
Suzukawa"One finished tsurugi requires one smith's life. Naturally a precious thing. The manufacturer himself has gone inside the product."
Yoshida"Sir!"

ja.html:
鈴川「劔冑はそれだけの力を持っている。 　その劔冑の使い手を武者むしゃという」
鈴川「近代以前、武者は一握りの上級士族だけに 限られていたが……高野、それはなぜだ？」
高野「劔冑が貴重品だったからです」
鈴川「なぜ貴重品だった？」
高野「鍛冶師一人につきひとつしか造れなかった からです」
鈴川「そうだ。劔冑鍛冶は生涯一打ひとうち。 　なぜなら、劔冑を完成させるには鍛冶師が 自分の身魂を鎧に打ち込まなくてはならない ……これを『心鉄しんがねを通す』という」
鈴川「そうすることで初めて、劔冑は最強の武器 としての力を得……その力を使い手の意思に 応じて制御するための頭脳も備える。 　心鉄を通さなければただの上出来な鎧だ」
鈴川「つまり、劔冑を一領造るには鍛冶師が命を 一つ捧げなくてはならないわけだ。 　貴重品なのは当然だな」
吉田「先生っ」

en.html:
Suzukawa"What is it, Yoshida?"
Yoshida"Then does the smith die after making it?"
Suzukawa"...Difficult question. The smith's soul remains as the armor's OS. Seen that way, zinda hai, you could say. Still alive."
Suzukawa"But as a component. A mind—or something like a mind—inside the armor. Humanity, almost entirely gone. Orders it answers. On its own initiative, nothing. Do not hear 'alive' and imagine the same life continuing."
Suzukawa"Some say there were once tsurugi that were different. Stories from the far side of legend. Probably none remain today."
Suzukawa"Chalo. That is why, until the modern age, warriors were so few."
Suzukawa"This was true worldwide. Then, National Year 2549: Ziegler, the arms maker in the Habsburg Dual Empire, completed a tsurugi without consuming its smith's life. First time in the world. An extraordinary change."

鈴川「どうした、吉田」
吉田「劔冑を造った鍛冶師は死ぬんですか？」
鈴川「……難しい質問だな。 　鍛冶師の心魂は劔冑の統御機能ＯＳとして残る わけだから、生きているという見方もできる」
鈴川「だがそれはあくまで、劔冑の部品としての 精神……というか、精神のようなもの・・・・・だ。 　人間らしさはほぼ無くしている。使用者の 命令に応えるだけで、自発的行動はしない」
鈴川「そうではない劔冑が嘗かつてあったという人も いるが、伝説の彼方の話だ。 　現代には残っていないだろう」
鈴川「さて。 　そういうわけで、近代まで、武者は非常に 数少なかった」
鈴川「世界共通のこの事情が劇的に変化するのは 国紀二五四九年……二重帝国ハプスブルクの兵器メーカー、 ゼグラー社が世界で初めて、鍛冶師の生命を 消費せずに劔冑を完成させた時のことだ」

en.html:
Suzukawa"Before that, 2544. What happened? Anyone knows?"
Tadayasu"Ji."
Suzukawa"Inagi."
Tadayasu"Professor Follett of the British Commonwealth was developing cloning technology by the Mirror method. The work stalled, and he sold his results to Ziegler."
Suzukawa"Results, matlab what exactly?"
Tadayasu"A replica human body. Body ban gaya, sir. The immune problem did not get solved. So the medical uses they had hoped for were judged impossible."
Suzukawa"Correct. Then Doctor Albrecht at Ziegler thought of using the technology to make tsurugi."
Suzukawa"The smith's body and soul serve two needs: a source of power, and intelligence to control that power. Dono chahiye. Both are required."
Suzukawa"For the first, he successfully substituted a replica body. For the second, a mechanical CPU and a program."
Suzukawa"A completely new tsurugi, which could be mass-produced. At last, the fellow making it could survive to make another."

ja.html:
鈴川「これに先立つ二五四四年。 　何があったか知っている者？」
忠保「はい」
鈴川「稲城」
忠保「大英連邦ブリテンのフォレット教授が研究していた 多重複写ミラー法による生体複製クローン技術開発が頓挫、 研究成果をゼグラー社に売却しました」
鈴川「成果とは具体的に？」
忠保「複製人体コピーボディの完成です。 　ただこれは、免疫問題を克服できなかった ため、期待されていた医療面での有効活用は 不可能と断定されました」
鈴川「そう。 　だがゼグラー社のアルブリヒト博士はこの 技術を劔冑の製造工程に転用することを思い ついたわけだ」
鈴川「劔冑は能力の源泉とするため、そして能力 を制御する知能とするために、鍛冶師自身の 心身を必要とする」
鈴川「それを博士は前者を複製人体、後者を機械 式の演算装置ＣＰＵと命令系プログラムで代用することに成功」
鈴川「量産可能な全く新しい劔冑を誕生させた」

en.html:
Suzukawa"Now, performance. The new type was far inferior to the old."
Suzukawa"A good old-type piece, for example, can receive an order and act independently even when nobody is wearing it. Most commonly it takes a horse's form, useful for travel."
Suzukawa"The new type cannot do that. But what it could do was quite sufficient."
Suzukawa"More importantly, no need to consume a valuable technician. Arre, the military men of every country sat up. The smith remaining available was a marvelous new feature."
Suzukawa"Countries raced to adopt it. Take the technology, mass-produce, improve. Phir improve some more."
Suzukawa"Many now say its performance is approaching the old type. There are even derivatives such as racing crucibles."
Suzukawa"As new-type use increased, old-type manufacture fell just as rapidly. Naturally. Give a man the option of not dying at work and see how popular it becomes."
Suzukawa"The knowledge scattered. Today, they say, the forging method survives only among a few smiths of the dwarf race."
Suzukawa"The new type now dominates the battlefield. Officers from distinguished families are about the only ones still using the old."
Suzukawa"Now, the names. Dhyaan do. Unless a failing mark is your personal ambition, listen properly."

Arre, close call.

I had nearly fallen asleep again. The history of the world's strongest weapon, and my eyelids had almost defeated it. No expensive research, no railgun. Just close slowly and the entire military problem goes away.

Then the examination comes, and you discover the weapon was stronger after all.

en.html:
Suzukawa"Back to the boundary between modern and contemporary history. Why begin the contemporary age with the dragoon? Okawa."
Ookawa"I don't know!"
Suzukawa"Excellent energy. Stand and preserve it. Now, our tsurugi expert, Inagi."
Tadayasu"The strongest weapon had belonged only to the powerful. Ab ordinary citizens could get their hands on it too."
Suzukawa"Correct. The new technology increased the number of tsurugi enormously—"
Suzukawa"Compared with before. Ten suits still requires a discussion at national-budget level. Enormously does not mean the corner shop is stocking them. They remain rare."
Suzukawa"More armor, not enough warriors from the warrior class. Where to get the rest? Commoners."
Suzukawa"Previously supporting players in the military, commoners were given tsurugi and formed dragoon units. Power comes into a man's hands, toh naturally his voice also starts carrying farther."
Suzukawa"Dragoon units in Yamato's military: Koryu 2. The property qualification for voting abolished: Koryu 10, National Year 2569. Only eight years between them. Coincidence? Nahin."
Suzukawa"They say guns gave birth to democracy. Then the new-type tsurugi brought it up. This is the thinking behind starting contemporary history with the dragoon."

ja.html:
鈴川「話を近代と現代の区分に戻すぞ。 　つまり竜騎兵の登場をもって現代の皮切り とする説があるわけだが、その理由はわかる か？　大川」
大川「わかりません！」
鈴川「元気があってよろしい。立ってろ。 　じゃあ劔冑博士の稲城」
忠保「それまで権力者の占有物だった最強兵器が、 市民階級の手にも渡るようになったからです」
鈴川「そうだ。 　新技術の誕生によって劔冑の数量が爆発的 に増え――」
鈴川「と言っても十領造るだけで国家予算レベル の検討が必要になる、依然として希少な品で あることに変わりはないんだがな。 　あくまでそれ以前との比較の話だ」
鈴川「劔冑の数量が増えると、使い手を士族階級 だけでまかなうわけにもいかなくなった。 　足りない分はどうする？　そう、平民だ」
鈴川「それまで軍においては脇役でしかなかった 平民層出身者が劔冑を与えられ、竜騎兵部隊 を構成してゆく。 　そうして力を持てば当然、発言力も増す」
鈴川「大和国軍における竜騎兵部隊の誕生が興隆 二年、選挙法から財産制限が撤廃されたのが 興隆十年……国紀二五六九年。この間わずか 八年というのは偶然でも何でもない」
鈴川「銃が民主主義を生んだという言葉があるが、 ならば育て上げたのは新型劔冑というわけだ。 　竜騎兵の登場をもって現代とするのはこの 考え方に由来する」

en.html:
Arre, what a bloodthirsty way to look at history.

Improve the weapons, change the whole age. Haan, probably that was one way of seeing it.

Then what weapon would start the next age?

Some fellow would make a bigger hole in somebody, and historians would all stand up: excellent, new chapter. The man with the hole would not be contributing to the discussion.

Bhai, I didn't like the sound of the question, never mind the answer.

en.html:
Suzukawa"As democracy and nationalism grew, people under colonial rule resisted the great powers. Resistance movements spread."
Suzukawa"Yamato responded by calling internationally for racial discrimination to be abolished. It wanted to establish itself as Asia's leader. The British Commonwealth and the other white powers objected."
Suzukawa"Even the Yamato-Russian War did not finally stop Russia advancing south. Yamato pushed onto the continent to counter it."
Suzukawa"The Commonwealth grew still more alarmed. And so, toward the Great War..."
Suzukawa"At home, the arrival of dragoons expanded the Rikuefu, the organization overseeing warriors. Before entering the war, it formed a national force alongside the Army and Navy. The Dragoon Army, commanding the capital region."
Suzukawa"...Our Rokuhara Shogunate was born."
Suzukawa"Then the Great War. Europe, Asia, elsewhere—war began. Yamato advanced onto the continent and into the South Seas. At first, victory after victory. Bas, a little more, and Asia would be united, it seemed."
Suzukawa"But the Commonwealth sent its New World garrison toward the Pacific to meet Yamato. It also moved the International League—"
Suzukawa"The International League for Unified Peace and Co-Prosperity. Founded to settle disputes peacefully. In practice, as you know, the Commonwealth and its satellite states agreeing with the Commonwealth. Bahut unified."
Suzukawa"With a League resolution, the Commonwealth formed the UNF. Its own New World troops remained the core, so the increase in fighting strength was not great. But the supply worry was removed. That mattered enormously."
Suzukawa"Yamato, meanwhile: few resources, no foreign help. Win quickly, win decisively—that plan failed, and there was nothing to keep it going. The front stalled..."
Suzukawa"Yamato's forces were pushed back, lost occupied territory, and finally had to fight on home soil. Still losing. Kyushu invaded, then Chugoku... but Rokuhara's army was intact."
Suzukawa"Everyone believed: bas, let Rokuhara take the field. Everything would turn around. And Rokuhara—"
Suzukawa"Made a historic decision. No precedent in all of Yamato."
Yuhi"..."

鈴川「民主主義あるいは民族主義の成長は大国の 植民地支配に対する被支配地域の反発を生み、 各地で抵抗運動が盛んになる」
鈴川「これを受ける格好で大和は人種差別思想の 撤廃を国際社会に訴え、アジアの盟主として の地位を確立しようと図ったが、大英連邦を 始め白人諸国の反発を買う」
鈴川「ロシアの南下は和露戦争によっても結局は 止められず、大和はこれに対抗する形で大陸 進出を推進」
鈴川「このことが大英連邦を更に警戒させ、大戦 へとつながっていく……」
鈴川「国内では竜騎兵の誕生により、武者統括の 組織であった六衛府りくえふが勢力を拡大。 　大戦突入に先立って陸軍・海軍と並ぶ国軍 組織を形成、竜軍と称して首都圏を統監した」
鈴川「……六波羅幕府の誕生だ」
鈴川「そして大戦。欧州、アジア、その他の地域 でも戦争の火蓋が切って落とされた。 　大和軍は大陸と南洋へ進出し、序盤は連戦 連勝、アジア統一も間近かと思われた」
鈴川「が、大英連邦は新大陸駐留軍を太平洋方面 へ向け、大和軍を迎撃させた。 　更には国際連盟を動かし――」
鈴川「国際統和共栄連盟は国家間問題の平和的な 解決を目的として創られた組織だが、実質、 大英連邦とその衛星国家による協賛会でしか ないのは皆も知っている通りだ」
鈴川「大英連邦は連盟の決議を得て連盟軍ＵＮＦを編成。 　戦力の中心はあくまでも自前の新大陸軍で、 そう増強されたわけでもないが、これにより 補給の不安が解消されたことの意味は大きい」
鈴川「一方、資源に恵まれず、他国からの支援も ない大和側は、速戦即決の意図を挫かれると 後が続かなかった。 　戦線は膠着し……」
鈴川「やがて大和軍は押し戻され、占領地を失い、 遂には本土決戦を迎える。 　敗勢はなおも続き、九州、中国と侵略され ……しかしまだ、六波羅軍は健在だった」
鈴川「誰もが、六波羅さえ出撃すれば状勢は覆る と信じていた……。 　そして六波羅は」
鈴川「大和史上に前例のない、歴史的決断を下す」
雄飛「…………」

ja.html: 絶妙な皮肉だった。
ja.text: 絶妙な皮肉だった。

en.html:
Suzukawa"Rokuhara betrayed us."
Suzukawa"Abandoned the homeland. Surrendered to the League. Then marched at the front of the League's forces to subdue Yamato. Towns burned. Citizens killed. Whatever resisted, destroyed. Apne hi log. Their own people."
Suzukawa"So the war ended. Yamato kept a nominal guarantee of sovereignty, but came under the League's GHQ. And for changing sides, Rokuhara was rewarded with the right to govern beneath it."
Suzukawa"Koryu 35. National Year 2594. Western Year 1934. ...Six years ago."
Suzukawa"Haan. Only six years. That is all the time that has passed."

ja.html:
鈴川「六波羅は裏切った・・・・・・・・」
鈴川「祖国を見捨て、連盟軍に降伏した。 　その尖兵となって、大和を制圧した。町を 焼き、市民を殺し、逆らう全てを滅ぼした」
鈴川「かくして大戦は終わり、大和は一応の主権 を保障されながらも、連盟の進駐軍司令部ＧＨＱの 管理下に置かれ……六波羅は寝返りの褒美に その下で大和の統治権を獲得する」
鈴川「時に、興隆三五年。国紀二五九四年。外暦 一九三四年。 　……今から六年前のことだ」
鈴川「そうだ。 　あれからまだ、六年しか・・・・経っていないのだ」
